summary: PS nanoplastics with H. pylori altered gastric cancer cell apoptosis, autophagy and mitochondrial potential; PS nanoplastics alone promoted liver and lung metastasis in nude mice.
Gold-coated fluorescent polystyrene nanosystem targeting ZIP4 for pancreatic cancer drug delivery and imaging; polymer used only as a carrier.
Polystyrene microplastics co-exposed with Vibrio harveyi raised liver enzymes, immune gene expression and caspase 8 in seahorses, with greater bacterial load in kidney.
Microplastics released from dentures and resin grinding were detected in dental clinics and showed toxicity to oral keratinocytes and inflammation in macrophages.
Optimised multistep digestion protocol for extracting and identifying microplastics in human tissues by micro-Raman; analytical method with no health endpoint.
Polystyrene microplastics in MIN6 beta cells caused dose-dependent ROS rise, necrosis and loss of beta-cell identity markers, implicating microplastics in beta-cell dysfunction.
Oral polystyrene microplastics disrupted hepatic and adipose lipid, glucose and amino acid metabolism in wild-type and leptin knockout mice, confirmed in HepG2 and 3T3-L1 cells.
Prospective clinical evaluation and treatment of chronic bowel symptoms after cancer treatment in colon and pelvic organs; no plastics involved.
Survey of microplastic accumulation in organs of Adelie penguins in Antarctica; wildlife survey with no health endpoint.
Biocompatibility of profiled PET and PVDF sutures in rats; bulk polymer implants with no particles studied.
Co-exposure to 50 and 500 nm polystyrene particles caused greater intestinal barrier dysfunction in mice than single sizes, via ROS-mediated epithelial apoptosis.
Rapid systematic review concluding microplastics are suspected to harm digestive, reproductive and respiratory health, with evidence unclassifiable for birth outcomes.
PET nanoplastics increased gastric cancer cell proliferation, migration and tumour growth in mice, inhibiting TNF-alpha/JAK1/STAT1 signalling and promoting an immunosuppressive microenvironment.
Immune-modifying polystyrene and PLGA microparticles used therapeutically to divert inflammatory monocytes in mouse disease models; particles used as a treatment tool.
Commentary on soil, water and plastic pollution, including micro- and nanoplastics, as an under-recognised contributor to cardiovascular disease and a target for prevention policy.
Chronic sediment exposure to PET fragments at two concentrations had little effect on Gammarus fossarum group size, oxygen consumption or proteome.
Pluronic-grafted culture dishes suppressing colon cancer stem cells while selecting adipose-derived stem cells; polymer used as a culture surface.
Gavaged micro- and nanoplastics disrupted thyroid architecture and hormones in mice, with NF-kB-driven NLRP3 pyroptosis in follicular cells, nanoplastics more potent.
Systematic review of nanoplastic effects in fish, reporting tissue accumulation, oxidative stress, neurotoxicity, immune and endocrine effects, mostly from polystyrene in zebrafish.
Ozone-aged polystyrene microplastics accumulated in mouse liver, gonads and spleen and, in females only, raised oestradiol and activated hepatic AMPK, reducing lipid synthesis.
Polystyrene nanoparticles aggravated DEHP-induced intestinal damage, mucus loss, tight junction disruption and gut microbiota changes across intestinal segments in mice.
PET/CTA imaging of muscle inflammation from cholesterol crystal emboli in rabbits; polystyrene microspheres used only as a control embolus.
Survey of microplastics in gut and lungs of free-living opossums in Brazil; wildlife survey with no tissue damage found.
Microplastics released from syringes, infusion sets and venous needles were characterised, and annual intravenous intake per person was estimated.
Review of interactions between micro(nano)plastics and the gut microbiota, including dysbiosis and possible microbial biodegradation of ingested particles.
